egress.terms: the billing page states that only outbound traffic is charged, that inbound is not charged, that the basic allowance is 2,400GB on a leased server with 70 per GB above it billed the following month, and that the connection is not throttled when the allowance is exceeded

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: The no-throttle policy makes CLOUDV different from the rest of the Korean market: every other host found either throttles or stops at the allowance, and CLOUDV turns an overrun into an invoice instead.

limits.value: 1,200 GB of monthly outbound, then KRW 70 per GB with no bandwidth throttle, which means an unattended job that moves a terabyte over the allowance adds KRW 70,000 to the invoice instead of failing.

record.notes: CLOUDV is the cloud brand of SmileServ, the same company that runs iwinv, so the two records describe one operator at two price points: iwinv is the per-day shared line at KRW 5,600, CLOUDV is the monthly RAID-backed box at KRW 31,500. Prices exclude VAT. The vendor also lists bare-metal leases by the month with a 24-month term, which are not virtual machines and are recorded here only as the shape above them.
